info.title: Filinq Register
info.description: Filinq register v8.16.0: leaf-integrations. Six schemas opt into the standard OpenRegister leaves through `configuration.linkedTypes`: `signingRequest` (mail, calendar), `signerRecord` (contacts), `publicationConsent` (mail, calendar, deck), `correspondence` (mail), `generatedDocument` (files) and `dossier` (files, deck). `publicationConsent` and `correspondence` also carry a `mailObjectTemplate`, so an objection mail or an inbound case mail can seed a record from the NC Mail sidebar, in its initial state and nothing further. Every template key was cross-checked against that schema’s own `properties` map, because an unknown key fails the whole register import. No property, `required` list or authorization block changes, and the agent-facing MCP surface is untouched. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.15.0: redaction-and-what-leaves-the-building, the verdict. `anonymizationLink` moves to 1.1.0 and carries the irreversibility verifier's answer about the bytes that were actually written: `verificationVerdict` (clean, leaking or unverifiable), `verificationOutputMode`, `verificationRoutes`, `verificationLeakRoutes` and `verifiedAt`. The verdict is recorded even when it is `unverifiable`, because an empty field and a clean verdict look the same to anything filtering on "was this copy checked" and one of them means nobody looked. The output mode is stored beside the verdict because a PDF/UA rewrite can put a text layer back: the answer holds for the mode that produced this copy and for no other. THE BUMP IS THE POINT AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC HERE: this schema is `hardValidation: true`, so on an install that has not re-imported, the five new fields are undeclared and OpenRegister REFUSES the whole link write, which loses the source-to-copy pairing rather than only the verdict. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.14.0: intake-failure-reaches-someone. `intakeDocument` gains `readingState`, `readingError` and `readingUpdatedAt`, and an `x-openregister-notifications` rule that tells the registrars when documents could not be read. The rule coalesces on an hour window and digests at 08:30, so a scanner jamming at 02:00 produces one message rather than one per page. It is addressed to docudesk-woo-officers, which ships EMPTY like every declared group: openregister now refuses a recipient that can never resolve at declaration time and records a rule that reached nobody at dispatch, once per run, so an unstaffed group is visible rather than silent. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.13.0: erase-a-person-while-the-records-stay. Adds `subjectErasureRequest`, a betrokkene asking to come out of the documents while the dossiers stay, carrying its own progress so an interrupted run resumes instead of restarting; and `erasureCertificate`, which names the refusals as prominently as the erasures and names separately anything already published that still carries the person. The certificate declares create and read for privacy officers and policy admins and NO update or delete: a certificate that can be amended afterwards records what somebody wanted it to say. Both carry an authorization cascade and a retention; the erasure is declared as its own x-openregister-processing activity. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.12.0: three-service-written-schemas-restrict-create. `signingAuditEntry.create` is restricted to docudesk-signing-admins: nothing writes that schema any more (the entries migrated to OpenRegister audit and its config keys are deprecated), so restricting it breaks no path while removing a forgeable signing-history shape. `anonymizationLink` and `documentVersion` were examined and LEFT OPEN, with the reason recorded on each: both are written from #[NoAdminRequired] endpoints by ordinary users and neither write passes `_rbac: false`, so restricting create would fail the anonymise and the finalisation for every user outside the group, which is what restricting prohibitionOverrideAudit.create did in v7.7.0. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.11.0: redaction-and-what-leaves-the-building. Adds `redactionReviewMark`, the record that a person looked at THIS detection run and agreed the redacted copy may be written, and `downloadAgreement`, the terms a download is gated on with who accepted them and when. The mark binds to a detection run rather than to a document: re-running detection leaves the old mark covering findings nobody has looked at, so the gate compares the run and refuses. It records `detectorVersion` so that after a fleet-wide model upgrade it is possible to ASK which approved documents were checked under the old model; an upgrade does not invalidate existing marks, because doing so silently would refuse thousands of already-approved documents in one night. Both schemas declare an authorization cascade: an omitted cascade is OPEN in OpenRegister, and on a review mark that would let any authenticated user sign the approval for their own document. Creating a mark is restricted to docudesk-woo-officers and docudesk-policy-admins. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.10.0: scan-intake-with-separator-sheets. Adds `scanBatch`, one PDF as a scanner delivered it, with an `x-openregister-lifecycle` whose terminal states are `split` and `failed`. A batch that cannot be read fails rather than arriving as one document nobody notices. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.9.0: merge-documents-to-pdf. Adds `mergeJob`, one request to turn several documents into one ordered PDF, with an `x-openregister-lifecycle` on `status` whose terminal states are `done` and `failed`. A failed merge leaves no partial file. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.8.0: documents-from-a-template. Three schemas are added: `pageLayout`, versioned so a layout edited in April cannot rewrite a besluit sent in March; `periodicDocument`, a template rendered over a saved view on a cadence; and `archiveJob`, one bundle of every file on an object with a manifest of what went in and what was left out. `generatedDocument` moves to 1.1.0 and records the layout version it used, the view it rendered over and the review date it falls due on. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.7.0: case-documents-and-the-flat-list. `documentVersion` moves to 1.1.0 and carries `domains[]` and `createdByUser`, so one document serves several domains instead of being copied per domain, and a record whose last domain link is removed stays with its creator. A new `uploadPolicy` schema says what may be uploaded, and one standard policy is seeded. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.6.0: inbound-documents-and-the-worklist. `intakeDocument` moves to 1.1.0 and grows `arrivedWith` (an attachment names the message it came with), `stampedDefaults` and `defaultRule` (what was stamped at creation and which rule chose it), `partySuggestion` (read out of the text, never written as a party), `routing` and `acceptance`, a reading progress, and a `detached` state with the reason and the person who detached it, so a document taken off a record lands on a worklist instead of nowhere. Three schemas are added: `intakeDefaultRule`, `intakeRoutingRule` and `intakePartyCorrection`, the corpus every next party suggestion is ranked against. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.5.0: adds `intakeDocument` for document-intake-inbox, one object per document that arrived before anyone knew which record it belongs to, with an `x-openregister-lifecycle` on `status` whose initial state is `received` and whose terminal states are `assigned` and `rejected`; two waiting examples are seeded so the inbox is not empty on a fresh install. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.4.0: marks the `template` schema shareable (`configuration.x-openregister-shareable`), so OpenRegister's federated configuration sharing offers document templates as a shareable type with no Filinq code; `template` moves 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 so the change reaches existing installs. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.3.0: adds `documentVersion` and `documentFinalityRule` for final-documents-frozen. `documentVersion` is the finalisation record of one document version, carrying an `x-openregister-lifecycle` with a terminal `final` state; it stores no file bytes and no version history, so document-versions keeps Nextcloud files_versions as the only version store. `documentFinalityRule` records which states of a consuming app's record type make its documents final. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.1.0: retires the `product` schema. Pipelinq owns `product` for the fleet, and nothing in Filinq read this copy. It was one of three apps claiming the slug (decidiq, filinq, pipelinq), and on a shared instance a bare relation resolves by slug alone. Removing it from this descriptor is only half the job: the import unions schema ids, so the live row is removed with `occ openregister:schemas:prune-retired --app filinq --slug product --apply`. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.0.0 — ALL REGISTERS INTO ONE. The five registers this file used to declare (`consent`, `signing`, `templates`, `document`, `dossier`) are replaced by a single register `filinq` carrying all 23 schemas, matching `x-openregister.app`. A SIXTH source was added after the first pass: `docudesk`, the register named for this app's OLD APP ID, which holds 200 objects of this app's own data. It was initially left out as "not one of the five" — true, and beside the point: leaving it standing meant "five into one" quietly shipped an app that owned two registers. It is migrated LAST, so a partial failure that stops before it still leaves the coherent five together. THIS IS NOT A RENAME AND IT DOES NOT MIGRATE ITSELF: an object is bound to its register by NUMERIC id and lives in a per-pair shard table `<prefix>openregister_table_<registerId>_<schemaId>`, so the existing objects sit in tables the new register does not own. The repair step `OCA\Filinq\Repair\ConsolidateRegisters` physically moves them (insert into the target shard table, count the uuids back out, only then delete the source rows), refuses rather than overwrites on a uuid collision, and skips any pair whose target table the import has not created yet. The MAJOR bump is deliberate — the version gate in SettingsInitializer is strictly-greater, so without it nothing reaches an existing install. PREVIOUSLY, v7.11.0 — template-authoring-for-agents (rate card): adds the `product` schema to the `templates` register, exposing `filinq.product.search` + `.get` as DERIVED read tools via `configuration.x-openregister-mcp`. No PHP: the quotation flow composes from tools that already exist (`template.get` for the body, `client`/`lead` from pipelinq, `editDocument` to write into the file the user has open), so the only thing missing was priced data. ⚠️ THE POINT: measured 2026-08-17 across all 160 distinct tools on this instance, NOTHING resolved a product or a rate. Asked to quote "5 hours of dev work" a model has three options — ask, refuse, or invent — and an hourly rate is exactly the plausible-sounding fact it supplies unprompted. On a quotation that is the failure that costs money. The `search` description therefore instructs the agent to return ALL candidates and to ASK when there is no match, never to estimate: "dev work" matches several roles at different rates and picking one silently is how a quote goes out at the wrong price. Writes stay with `docudesk-template-editors` — a rate card is a commercial artefact, consistent with v7.8.0's decision that no Filinq schema exposes a derived create/update/delete verb. ALSO IN v7.11.0 — batch-state-persistence: adds the `anonymizationBatch` schema to the `document` register. Batch anonymisation state used to live ONLY in Nextcloud's distributed cache. `ICacheFactory::createDistributed()` degrades to the local cache class, and that defaults to `OC\Memcache\NullCache` whenever `memcache.local` is unset — which is every Nextcloud that has not been explicitly pointed at APCu/Redis/Memcached, including a stock `occ maintenance:install`. NullCache discards every write and returns null for every read, so the batch record vanished the instant the creating request ended: `POST /api/anonymization/batch/folder` answered 200 with a batchId and fileCount 2, and the very next call `POST /api/anonymization/batch/{id}/extract` answered 404 `Batch not found or expired` (CI run 31963162253). That is the entire multi-file anonymisation flow, broken on every install without a distributed cache. Per ADR-022/ADR-083 the record is now persisted through OpenRegister's object abstraction (BatchStateRepository), with the cache demoted to a read fast path, so the flow is correct with no cache configured at all. `hardValidation:false` because the per-document progress entries evolve with the extraction pipeline and a validation refusal here would re-break the very flow this schema exists to keep working; the batch is app-private transient state, not a record anyone else reads. No `x-openregister-archival` annotation: batches are working state and MUST stay deletable, and an archival annotation makes user-driven deletes throw ArchivalImmutableException. The `authorization` cascade follows v7.9.0's shape rather than being omitted — an omitted cascade is OPEN in OpenRegister, so shipping this schema without one would have re-opened exactly the hole v7.9.0 closed, on a record that lists a user's private filenames. Filinq's own reads and writes go through `_rbac: false` (ownership is enforced in BatchStateService::getBatch), so the cascade governs only direct OpenRegister API access. ⚠️ THE VERSION BUMP IS THE POINT — SettingsInitializer gates the import on `info.version` against the stored `configuration_version`, so a new schema shipped WITHOUT a bump never reaches an existing install and every batch there keeps 404-ing. Previous v7.9.0 — consumer-schema-authorization-audit: declares an `authorization` cascade on ALL 21 schemas. Before this, 20 of 21 declared none, and OpenRegister treats an unconfigured cascade as OPEN — `PermissionHandler::resolveAuthorization()` returns null and every caller is admitted. The Filinq registers carry no register-level cascade either (measured live: all three rows NULL), so nothing filled the gap. MEASURED ON THE DEV INSTANCE BEFORE THE CHANGE, with two ordinary users in no groups and the same organisation: ddauth-bob read ddauth-alice's private template (HTTP 200, full `content`), OVERWROTE its content via PUT (HTTP 200), and duplicated it. This is a WRITE exposure, not only disclosure. The bound is authenticated users within one organisation — multitenancy is a separate axis and stays enforced; it is not anonymous and not cross-tenant. Shape of the fix: `update`/`delete` are restricted on EVERY schema, because that is where the proven harm was; OpenRegister's unconditional owner bypass means a creator keeps full control of their own objects, so this closes cross-user writes without an outage. `read` is additionally restricted only where the data justifies it — financialExtraction + glAccountBooking (supplier IBAN/KvK/BTW), publicationConsent + prohibitionOverrideAudit (GDPR records about identified people), and the four signing schemas (the signer portal resolves signerRecord with `_rbac: false` behind its own token binding in PortalSigningReceiverController, so restricting the cascade does NOT break the signer flow). Everything else keeps `read: authenticated` as a recorded decision, not an omission — reference data (base, customDictionary, glAccountMappingRule) and shared assets (template, huisstijl) must be readable to be applied. ⚠️ `prohibitionOverrideAudit.create` is deliberately `authenticated`, NOT policy-admins: v7.7.0 below records that restricting it re-breaks the fail-closed override path for the ordinary operator who performs the anonymise, raising 500 on every acknowledged override. Four groups are named — docudesk-template-editors, docudesk-policy-admins (already existed), docudesk-financial-admins, docudesk-signing-admins — and OpenRegister provisions declared groups create-only on import, ahead of the content-hash skip. They ship EMPTY on purpose: an empty group denies everyone except admins and object owners, which is the correct default and is immediately visible, rather than back-filling grants nobody chose. Previous v7.8.0 — filinq-mcp-adoption + document-editing-tools: declares `configuration.x-openregister-mcp` on 8 of 21 schemas (template, huisstijl, correspondence, generatedDocument, batchCorrespondenceJob, signingRequest, dossier, base) with `search` + `get` ONLY, `scope: read`, `readOnlyHint: true`. No Filinq schema exposes a derived create/update/delete verb: templates and huisstijl are governance artefacts, correspondence/generatedDocument/batch rows are audit records, and signingRequest is the legal spine of a signature process. The remaining 13 schemas stay off entirely (signature material, citizen contact data, re-identification links, extracted invoice content). Every declared `search.filters` entry was cross-checked against that schema's own `properties` map — an unknown filter fails the whole register import. `generatedDocument.format` additionally gains `docx`, which an agent document edit produces and which the enum predated. ⚠️ THE VERSION BUMP IS THE POINT: SettingsInitializer gates the import on `info.version` against the stored `configuration_version` app-config value, so a dialect change shipped WITHOUT a bump is inert on every existing install — the schemas keep their old configuration and not one derived tool appears, with no error anywhere. Measured on the dev instance before the bump: the four curated #[McpTool] tools were live while all 16 derived tools were absent. Previous v7.7.0 — prohibition-override-audit-schema: adds the `prohibitionOverrideAudit` schema to the `consent` register. `ProhibitionOverrideCommitter::writeAudit()` has always written to `register: consent, schema: prohibitionOverrideAudit`, and that schema was declared NOWHERE — `GET /apps/openregister/api/objects/consent/prohibitionOverrideAudit` answered 404 `Schema not found` while its sibling `publicationProhibition` answered 200 on the same freshly-seeded instance. The write is explicitly fail-closed ('If the audit write fails we MUST NOT proceed to the OR PATCH'), so every acknowledged override raised RuntimeException 500 and NO override could ever be committed. openspec/specs/anonymisation-prohibition-gate/spec.md mandates the schema by name: 'Implementations MUST use a `prohibitionOverrideAudit` schema in `filinq_register.json` for this entry'. Properties are exactly the six the committer writes {ruleId, entityRelationId, fileId, reason, acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedAt}; retention P10Y because an override audit must outlive the P10Y prohibition it released. `authorization: null` matches publicationConsent/anonymizationLink — restricting `create` to policy admins would re-break the same fail-closed path for the ordinary operator who performs the anonymise. See ConductionNL/filinq#428. Previous v7.6.4 — standing-consent-documentid-not-required: `publicationConsent` listed `documentId` in the schema-level `required` array, so OpenRegister created the backing column NOT NULL. Every scope=entity (standing consent) record is document-less by definition, so all 12 seeded standing consents failed to insert with 'null value in column "document_id" violates not-null constraint', and the same constraint blocks PolicyController::createStandingConsent at runtime — the entire "Publish always" surface. The condition is PER RECORD, not per schema, and openspec/specs/consent-management/spec.md already states it: 'documentId MUST be required only for scope=document records'. It is enforced where it can be — ConsentScopeValidator::assertValid(), which rejects a scope=document record without a documentId AND a scope=entity record WITH one. Removing it from the schema's `required` array restores what the spec mandates; nothing is left unvalidated. Previous v7.6.3 — archival-retention-object-shape: fixes six schemas that OpenRegister REJECTED on import, so they never existed on any fresh install. Five (correspondence, signingRequest, signerRecord, signingAuditEntry, batchCorrespondenceJob) declared `x-openregister-archival.retention` as a bare ISO-8601 STRING; OpenRegister's ArchivalAnnotationValidator requires an object `{ default: <duration>, rules?: [] }` and threw 'retention is required and must be an object'. The sixth (publicationProhibition) declared an authorization action `write`, which is not in OpenRegister's CRUD vocabulary (create, read, update, delete) — expanded to create/update/delete, preserving the intent that docudesk-policy-admins may write. ImportHandler catches a per-schema exception, logs it and continues, so the import still answered HTTP 200 'Import successful' while writing only 14 of 20 schemas — which left signing entirely non-functional (signingRequest/signerRecord/signingAuditEntry absent). anonymizationLink and financialExtraction already used the object form; this aligns the rest. No property, slug or retention DURATION changed. Previous v7.6.2 — schema-level-titles-en: re-authored the remaining Dutch schema-level `title` values to English — base 'Grondslag' -> 'Legal Basis', huisstijl 'Huisstijl Configuration' -> 'Branding Configuration' (schema slugs, property keys/titles, enums, descriptions unchanged). Dutch labels now live in l10n/nl.json for the display layer. See openspec/changes (fleet-wide schema-i18n titles rule). Previous v7.6.1 — schema-titles-en: re-authored all Dutch schema property `title` values to English (property names/keys unchanged); Dutch labels now live in l10n/nl.json for the display layer. See openspec/changes (fleet-wide schema-i18n titles rule). Previous v7.6.0 — document-output-destinations-and-bulk-retention: generatedDocument gains additive, nullable fileId/filePath properties, populated when a generation is stored to Files via the new DocumentStorageService (options.output.mode 'files'/'both' on generate, or the now-persisted async bulk job). hardValidation:false, so existing rows remain valid unchanged. See openspec/changes/document-output-destinations-and-bulk-retention/. Previous v7.5.0 — unified-search-provider: corrects the searchable opt-in so only navigable schemas (template, signingRequest) stay searchable and every other schema is searchable:false, keeping Filinq's contribution to OpenRegister's shared Unified Search provider free of dead/unnavigable results. Deep-link routing for template + signingRequest lives in src/manifest.json deepLinks[]. No bespoke OCP\Search\IProvider — org scoping inherited from openregister_objects. See openspec/changes/unified-search-provider/. Previous v7.4.0 — adds customDictionary + customDictionaryTerm to the document register per custom-dictionary-recognition: organisation-scoped, register-i18n-tagged term lists (label, description, colour, matchMode exact/caseInsensitive/wordBoundary, deferred fuzzy flag, active, calculated termCount) matched by CustomDictionaryMatchService and written into OpenRegister's shared entity catalogue as CUSTOM_DICTIONARY occurrences alongside Presidio/regex detections. Seeds one demo dictionary ("Projectnamen") with two demo terms. See openspec/changes/custom-dictionary-recognition/. Previous v7.3.0 — MERGE of Robert's anonimiseren-bij-de-bron work onto development: Woo Art. 5 grondslagen legenda A–S seed (base schema), standing-consent generic-term seeds (publicationConsent, entityType OTHER, notificationStatus skipped), entityType OTHER enum on publicationConsent/publicationProhibition, and EML→PDF assembly. Development schemas + dialect/RBAC fixes are preserved. Previous v5.10.0 — adds glAccountBooking (opaque per-tenant GL-account booking history, keyed by supplierIdentity, fed by the financial-extraction corrections endpoint) and glAccountMappingRule (admin-editable cold-start keyword/category → account rules, no seeded rows — Filinq ships no chart of accounts) to the document register, per ai-gl-account-suggestion. Both hardValidation:true. See openspec/changes/ai-gl-account-suggestion/. Previous v5.9.0 adds the financialExtraction schema to the document register: structured financial field-extraction results (supplier/IBAN/KvK/BTW, invoice number, dates, currency, totals + VAT breakdown, line items) with per-field confidence and an additive corrections[] tuning corpus, per financial-document-field-extraction. hardValidation:true; x-openregister-archival category shipped as an explicit placeholder pending selectielijst-manager sign-off (same pattern as anonymizationLink). See openspec/changes/financial-document-field-extraction/. Previous v5.8.0 declares validationStatus + validationFindings as x-openregister-calculations on generatedDocument (computation backend filinq.validation = DocumentValidationService) per document-validation-checks; the event-listener fallback dispatches the same service until OR's ADR-031 calculation runtime ships. Previous v5.7.0 declared the four AVG Art. 30 processing activities (anonymisation, OCR, metadata-enrichment, signing) as x-openregister-processing catalogue annotations on anonymizationLink, generatedDocument, base, and signingAuditEntry: each carries purpose (doelbinding), legal basis, NER data categories, backend identifier, retention reference taken from the existing x-openregister-archival annotations ("not declared" where absent), and opts the schema into OpenRegister's per-access read-logging (logReads:true, attribution.default referencing the activity code). Requires OpenRegister >= 0.2.14. See openspec/changes/processing-activity-export/. Previous v5.5.0 extended OR register-i18n adoption to the remaining user-facing string fields across templateVersion (name/description/changelog), huisstijl (name), base (name/description), correspondence (templateName), signingRequest (documentName), signingSession (documentName), signerRecord (displayName/declineReason), publicationConsent (notes/objectionReason/publicationDecision), publicationProhibition (primaryName/reason/notes), and batchCorrespondenceJob (templateName). OpenRegister TranslationHandler picks these up automatically and stores per-language variants under the existing object JSON column; no DB migration required. See openspec/changes/register-i18n/. Previous v5.4.0 tagged template (name/description/content/category) + dossier (name/description) per register-i18n. Previous v5.3.0 adopted OR abstractions per docudesk-adopt-or-abstractions, added batchCorrespondenceJob schema with x-openregister-lifecycle + archival + notifications + calculations, added x-openregister-archival to signingAuditEntry (P10Y), signingRequest (P10Y), signerRecord (P10Y), correspondence (P7Y), added x-openregister-lifecycle to signingSession, and added anonymizationLink schema for source↔anonymised file mapping.

filinq.title: Filinq Register
filinq.description: Eén register voor alle Filinq-objecten: GDPR/Woo publicatie-instemmingen en -verboden, digitale ondertekeningsverzoeken en -sessies, herbruikbare document templates met versiebeheer en rate card, correspondentie- en documentlogging, huisstijl, financiële veldextractie en grootboekrekening-suggesties, organisatie-woordenlijsten, anonimiseringsbatches, en dossiers met hun Woo Art. 5 grondslagen. VERVANGT de vijf registers `consent`, `signing`, `templates`, `document` en `dossier`; de bestaande objecten worden door de repair step OCA\Filinq\Repair\ConsolidateRegisters fysiek naar dit register verplaatst (insert-verify-delete per shard-tabel). De slug MOET gelijk blijven aan `x-openregister.app`: voor een `type: application` configuratie leest ImportHandler `$slug = $xOpenregister['app'] ?? $appId` en dat veld IS een register-slug, geen attributielabel.

documentRegistration.title: Document Registration
documentRegistration.description: One entry in the post register: a document that entered or left the building, the unit that registered it, and the number it was given. The number comes from a platform sequence, never from a counter in filinq, so two registrations made at the same moment cannot receive the same one.

direction.description: Whether the document came in or went out. There is no third value: a document that never left is not registered here at all.
direction.title: Direction

registeredAt.description: When the registration was made. This is the moment of registering, not the date printed on the document, and the two differ often enough that conflating them loses the post register's whole point.
registeredAt.title: Registered At

unit.description: The unit that registered it. The number series runs per unit, so this is what decides which sequence the number is drawn from.
unit.title: Unit

registrationNumber.description: The number this registration was given, drawn from a platform sequence and reset each year. Filinq keeps no counter: two registrations made in the same second would otherwise race for one number and one would silently reuse it. NOTE: the series is instance-wide, not per unit. OpenRegister builds the sequence scope as the literal sequence name plus the period, with no placeholder substitution, so a name like filinq-post-{unit} would create one shared series literally called that rather than one per unit. Per-unit series need platform support that does not exist yet.
registrationNumber.title: Registration Number

answers.description: For an outbound registration, the inbound one it answers. The discharge is READ FROM THIS LINK and is never written as a status on the inbound entry, so an inbound entry cannot be marked answered by anything except an actual answer existing.
answers.title: Answers

withdrawnReason.description: Why a number that was allocated was never used. An unexplained gap in a numbered series reads as a lost document; a gap with a reason reads as a decision, and the series stays legible end to end.
withdrawnReason.title: Withdrawn Reason

withdrawnAt.description: When the allocation was withdrawn. The reason says why and this says when, and a withdrawal with only one of the two is half a record: an auditor reading the series a year later needs to place the gap in time as well as explain it.
withdrawnAt.title: Withdrawn At

subject.nl: Bezwaartermijn verloopt binnenkort voor een publicatie
subject.en: Objection deadline is approaching for a publication

publicationConsent.title: Publication Consent
publicationConsent.description: Schema voor het beheren van publicatie toestemmingen volgens GDPR en Nederlandse Wet Open Overheid. Bevat informatie over entiteiten (personen/organisaties) die geïnformeerd moeten worden voordat een document wordt gepubliceerd, en hun reactie daarop.

scope.description: Discriminator: `document` = per-document/per-entity consent in the WOO workflow; `entity` = standing consent for a recurring entity (mayor, council member, etc.). Default `document` preserves backward compatibility: existing rows automatically load as `document`.
scope.title: Scope

documentId.description: Verwijzing naar het document dat gepubliceerd moet worden. Verplicht voor scope=document, VERBODEN voor scope=entity (standing consent) — die conditie is per record en wordt afgedwongen door ConsentScopeValidator, niet door dit schema. Zie openspec/specs/consent-management/spec.md: "documentId MUST be required only for scope=document records".
documentId.title: Document ID

entityType.description: Type entiteit (PERSON, ORGANIZATION of OTHER). OTHER maakt een standing-consent type-agnostisch: de regel matcht ongeacht welk type de detectie toekent (bijv. generieke termen die als PERSON of LOCATION herkend kunnen worden). Legacy/fallback: populated denormalised when no contactRef is set; once contactRef is linked, the contacts-leaf vCard is the source of truth for this field.
entityType.title: Entity type

entityText.description: Tekst van de gedetecteerde entiteit (Legacy/fallback: populated denormalised when no contactRef is set; once contactRef is linked, the contacts-leaf vCard is the source of truth for this field.)
entityText.title: Entity text

anonymizationBatch.title: Anonymisation Batch
anonymizationBatch.description: State of one multi-file anonymisation run: which documents it covers, how far each of them got, and which phase the batch as a whole is in. The batch flow spans several HTTP requests (create -> extract -> review -> anonymise -> report), so this record is what carries it between them. It was previously held only in Nextcloud's distributed cache, which degrades to a NullCache on any instance without `memcache.local` configured — the record was discarded on write and every follow-up call on the batch answered 404. Written and read exclusively by BatchStateRepository, keyed by the batch UUID (the object UUID is the batchId). Ownership is enforced in BatchStateService::getBatch(), which refuses a batch belonging to another non-admin user.

anonymizationLink.title: Anonymisation Link
anonymizationLink.description: create is `authenticated` DELIBERATELY. The link is written by AnonymizationPersistenceService during an anonymise, which ordinary operators perform through #[NoAdminRequired] endpoints, and that write does not pass `_rbac: false`, so the acting user is the operator. Restricting create to a group would fail the write for every operator outside it, which is exactly what restricting prohibitionOverrideAudit.create did in v7.7.0: 500 on every use of a fail-closed path. Closing the forgery route means making the write system-asserted first; that is a service change with the #283 caveat, not a cascade edit. Koppeling tussen een bronbestand (niet-geanonimiseerd) en zijn geanonimiseerde tegenhanger. Eén record per bronbestand (idempotent op sourceFileId); her-anonimisering werkt hetzelfde record bij. documentVersion.title: Document version
documentVersion.description: create is `authenticated` DELIBERATELY, for the same reason as anonymizationLink: FinalDocumentRepository::save() is reached from #[NoAdminRequired] endpoints when an ordinary user finalises a document, and it does not pass `_rbac: false`. Restricting create would break finalisation for everyone outside the group. The finalisation record of one version of a document. A version is draft or final. Final records who made it final, when, why, and the checksum of the file at that moment. This schema holds no file content and no version history: the bytes stay in Nextcloud files_versions, which document-versions keeps as the only version store.

fileId.description: Nextcloud file id of the document this version belongs to.
fileId.title: File ID

versionLabel.description: The files_versions label this record is about. Empty means the current content.
versionLabel.title: Version label

documentName.description: Name of the document when the record was written.
documentName.title: Document name

status.description: Draft or final. Final is terminal: a final version accepts no write and no way back.
status.title: Status

finalisedBy.title: Finalised by

finalReason.description: The reason or the act that made this version final, such as the decision that was taken.
finalReason.title: Reason

supersedes.description: UUID of the final version this one corrects. The superseded version stays readable and stays final.
supersedes.title: Supersedes

supersededBy.description: UUID of the version that corrects this one, written on the predecessor so a reader of either sees the chain.
supersededBy.title: Superseded by

fileChecksum.description: sha256 of the file at the moment it became final. A later mismatch means the file changed outside Filinq.
fileChecksum.title: File checksum

unfrozen.description: True once an administrator has unfrozen this version. The mark is permanent and cannot be cleared.
unfrozen.title: Unfrozen

Filinq does not define the record type vocabulary: dossiq owns its case types and result types, and this schema only records what that app declared.

finalStates.description: The states of that record type that make its documents final.
finalStates.title: Final states

documentRole.description: Which document of the record the rule applies to, such as besluit. Empty means every document of the record.
documentRole.title: Document role

reasonTemplate.description: The reason written on the version when this rule fires. Empty means the transition itself is the reason.

declaredBy.description: User id that stored the declaration.
declaredBy.title: Declared by

intakeDocument.title: Intake document
intakeDocument.description: A document that arrived before anyone knew which record it belongs to. It waits in the intake inbox until a clerk assigns it to a record or rejects it with a reason. The channel that delivered it never assigns it. An attachment is a record of its own and names the message it arrived with. A document taken off a record comes back here as detached, with the reason.

channel.description: How the document reached the organisation: a scanner, a mailbox or digital post.
channel.title: Channel

subject.description: Subject line or document title as the channel delivered it.
subject.title: Subject

file.title: File

fileName.description: Name of the received file at the moment it arrived.
fileName.title: File name

sourceRef.description: The reference the channel itself uses, such as a message id or a scan batch number. Keeps a second delivery of the same document from becoming a second intake document.
sourceRef.title: Source reference

status.description: Where the document stands: waiting for a clerk, assigned to a record, rejected, or taken back off a record and waiting again.

routing.description: The group this document was routed to on arrival, taken from the record type the consuming app declared it against.
routing.title: Routing

acceptance.description: Whether the routed group still has to accept this document, and who accepted it.
acceptance.title: Acceptance

classificationProgress.description: How far the background reading of this document has come, from 0 to 100. A document still being read is listed in the inbox with its progress rather than hidden.

intakeDefaultRule.description: Says what metadata an arriving document is stamped with before any classifier looks at it, matched on the channel it came through or on its sender. Nothing arrives unclassified, and every stamped value names the rule that chose it.

intakeRoutingRule.title: Intake routing rule
intakeRoutingRule.description: What a consuming app declared about inbound documents on one of its record types: who they go to, and whether somebody has to accept them. Filinq stores and applies the declaration; the record type vocabulary stays the consumer's.

declaringApp.description: App id of the consuming app that made the declaration, such as dossiq. Filinq does not define the record type vocabulary.

routeTo.description: The group an inbound document on this record type goes to. Empty means no routing.

active.title: Active

periodicDocument.title: Periodic document

subject.description: The object whose files were bundled, as register, schema and id.
subject.title: Subject

requestedBy.title: Requested by

ceilingBytes.description: The administered ceiling in force for this job, in bytes.

includedCount.description: How many files went into the archive.

redactionReviewMark.title: Redaction Review Mark
redactionReviewMark.description: Het bewijs dat een mens de gedetecteerde entiteiten van DIT detectie-uitvoering heeft bekeken en akkoord is dat de geredigeerde kopie geschreven mag worden. Detectie is een oordeel van een machine over waar de namen staan; het besluit dat deze kopie het pand mag verlaten is van een mens. De markering hoort bij een detectie-uitvoering, niet bij het document: wordt de detectie opnieuw gedraaid, dan is de markering van de vorige uitvoering en dekt zij de nieuwe bevindingen niet.

document.description: Het document waarvan de geredigeerde kopie geschreven mag worden.

detectionRun.description: De detectie-uitvoering die is bekeken. De markering dekt alleen deze uitvoering.

checkedBy.description: Wie het heeft gecontroleerd. Een controle die niemand heeft ondertekend is een controle waarover niemand bevraagd kan worden.
checkedBy.title: Checked By

detectorVersion.description: De versie van het detectiemodel dat deze uitvoering heeft geproduceerd. Vastgelegd zodat na een vlootbrede modelupgrade te vinden is welke goedgekeurde documenten onder het oude model zijn gecontroleerd. Een upgrade laat bestaande markeringen staan: ze zijn geldig voor hun eigen uitvoering, en het automatisch ongeldig verklaren zou duizenden reeds goedgekeurde documenten in een nacht weigeren.

subjectErasureRequest.title: Subject Erasure Request
subjectErasureRequest.description: Een verzoek van een betrokkene om uit de documenten te worden verwijderd, terwijl de dossiers zelf blijven bestaan. Anders dan een archivering, die start als een bewaartermijn afloopt, start dit als iemand een recht uitoefent: de betrokkene heeft deze documenten niet gekozen, en er loopt een wettelijke termijn. De voortgang staat op het verzoek zelf, zodat een afgebroken run hervat kan worden in plaats van opnieuw te beginnen.

identifiers.title: Identifiers
identifiers.description: Elke schrijfwijze waaronder deze persoon in documenten voorkomt. Eén naam vindt niet elk voorkomen.

requestedAt.description: Wanneer het verzoek binnenkwam. De termijn loopt hiervandaan.
requestedAt.title: Requested At

progress.title: Progress
progress.description: Welke documenten al gedaan zijn, zodat een afgebroken run verdergaat waar hij stopte en niet opnieuw over alles loopt.

lastDocument.description: Het laatst voltooide document, het hervatpunt.

excluded.title: Excluded
excluded.description: Voorkomens die een behandelaar vóór de run heeft uitgesloten, met reden. Zonder reden is een uitsluiting niet te verantwoorden.

x-openregister-archival.reason: Het verzoek is het bewijs dat iemand zijn recht heeft uitgeoefend en wat daarmee is gebeurd; het moet de behandeltermijn en een eventuele klacht overleven.

x-openregister-processing.purpose: Uitvoeren van een verwijderingsverzoek van een betrokkene, terwijl de dossiers blijven bestaan.
x-openregister-processing.legalBasis: AVG artikel 17, met artikel 17 lid 3 als grond voor de weigeringen.

erasureCertificate.title: Erasure Certificate
erasureCertificate.description: Wat er werkelijk is gewist, wat is geweigerd en waarom, en wat elders al gepubliceerd is en dus opnieuw gepubliceerd moet worden. Het certificaat noemt de weigeringen even prominent als de wissingen: een certificaat dat alleen opsomt wat is gewist leest als een afgerond verzoek.

erased.title: Erased
erased.description: Per document het aantal gewiste voorkomens.

refused.title: Refused
refused.description: Per geweigerd document de verplichting en wie erover beslist.

needsRepublishing.title: Needs Republishing
needsRepublishing.description: Reeds gepubliceerde kopieën die de persoon nog bevatten. Het volgende probleem van de verzoeker, dus apart genoemd.

objects.name: A — Eenheid van de Kroon
objects.description: Openbaarmaking kan de eenheid van de Kroon in gevaar brengen (art. 5.1 lid 1 a Woo — absolute uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: B — Veiligheid van de Staat
objects.description: Openbaarmaking kan de veiligheid van de Staat schaden (art. 5.1 lid 1 b Woo — absolute uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: C — Bedrijfs- en fabricagegegevens
objects.description: Betreft bedrijfs- en fabricagegegevens die vertrouwelijk aan de overheid zijn meegedeeld (art. 5.1 lid 1 c Woo — absolute uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: D — Bijzondere en strafrechtelijke persoonsgegevens
objects.description: Betreft bijzondere persoonsgegevens (par. 3.1) of persoonsgegevens van strafrechtelijke aard (par. 3.2) van de Uitvoeringswet AVG, waarvoor geen toestemming is gegeven of die de betrokkene niet kennelijk zelf openbaar heeft gemaakt (art. 5.1 lid 1 d Woo — absolute uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: E — Identificatienummers
objects.description: Betreft nummers die dienen ter identificatie van personen, bij wet of AMvB voorgeschreven als bedoeld in art. 46 Uitvoeringswet AVG, tenzij de verstrekking kennelijk geen inbreuk op de levenssfeer maakt (art. 5.1 lid 1 e Woo — absolute uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: F — Betrekkingen met andere staten
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen het belang van de betrekkingen van Nederland met andere staten en met internationale organisaties (art. 5.1 lid 2 a Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: G — Economische of financiële belangen van de Staat
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen de economische of financiële belangen van de Staat, andere publiekrechtelijke lichamen of bestuursorganen (art. 5.1 lid 2 b Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: H — Opsporing en vervolging van strafbare feiten
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen het belang van de opsporing en vervolging van strafbare feiten (art. 5.1 lid 2 c Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: I — Inspectie, controle en toezicht
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen het belang van de inspectie, controle en toezicht door bestuursorganen (art. 5.1 lid 2 d Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: J — Persoonlijke levenssfeer
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen het belang van de eerbiediging van de persoonlijke levenssfeer van betrokkenen (art. 5.1 lid 2 e Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond). Grondslag voor gewone persoonsgegevens.

objects.name: K — Concurrentiegevoelige bedrijfsgegevens
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen de bescherming van andere dan in art. 5.1 lid 1 sub c genoemde concurrentiegevoelige bedrijfs- en fabricagegegevens (art. 5.1 lid 2 f Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: L — Bescherming van het milieu
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen de bescherming van het milieu waar deze informatie betrekking op heeft (art. 5.1 lid 2 g Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: M — Beveiliging van personen en bedrijven
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen de beveiliging van personen en bedrijven en het voorkomen van sabotage (art. 5.1 lid 2 h Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: N — Goed functioneren van de Staat
objects.description: Het belang van openbaarmaking weegt niet op tegen het goed functioneren van de Staat, andere publiekrechtelijke lichamen of bestuursorganen (art. 5.1 lid 2 i Woo — relatieve uitzonderingsgrond).

objects.name: O — Geadresseerde eerst kennisnemen
objects.description: Het belang dat de geadresseerde erbij heeft om als eerste kennis te kunnen nemen van de informatie (tijdelijke beperking) (art. 5.1 lid 4 Woo).

objects.name: P — Onevenredige benadeling
objects.description: De onevenredige benadeling die, in uitzonderlijke gevallen, wordt toegebracht aan een ander belang dan genoemd in art. 5.1 leden 1 en 2, bij andere informatie dan milieu-informatie (art. 5.1 lid 5 Woo).

objects.name: Q — Milieu-informatie, ernstige schade
objects.description: Het belang genoemd in art. 5.1 lid 1 c, waarbij het milieu-informatie betreft waardoor bij openbaarmaking ernstige schade wordt toegebracht aan dat belang (art. 5.1 lid 6 Woo).

objects.name: R — Persoonlijke beleidsopvattingen
objects.description: Persoonlijke beleidsopvattingen: ambtelijke adviezen, visies, standpunten en overwegingen t.b.v. intern beraad, niet zijnde feiten, prognoses, beleidsalternatieven of onderdelen met een overwegend objectief karakter (art. 5.2 lid 1 Woo).

objects.name: S — Tot personen herleidbare beleidsopvattingen
objects.description: Tot personen te herleiden gegevens met betrekking tot door het bestuursorgaan, met het oog op goede en democratische bestuursvoering, verstrekte informatie die kwalificeert als persoonlijke beleidsopvattingen (art. 5.2 lid 2 Woo).
